name: BLUF error card
summary: Built around the failure. While running, a single transient status line shows '[n/6] step'. On success it prints a two-line result. On an expected failure it prints a bordered error card whose title is the bottom line (what failed), with step, cause, fix, done/not-run and a debug hint. Unexpected errors keep the traceback, but only with -d.
mockup:
SUCCESS (TTY, final frame)
pkgdx init: done in 2.9s
  changed: prek.toml (updated, 2 hooks added), .secrets.baseline (created)

(mid-run, transient)
⠼ pkgdx init  [5/6] prek update --check  1.1s

WARN (TTY, final frame)
pkgdx init: done in 2.9s with 2 warnings
  ! identify Git top-level: not a Git repository, using project root
      -> Run `git init` to enable pre-commit hooks
  ! prek update --check: pkgdx v0.4.2 -> v0.5.0 available
      -> Update remote hook revisions - `prek update`
  changed: nothing

FAIL (TTY, final frame)
╭─ error: pkgdx init failed at 'configure pre-commit hooks' ───────────────────────╮
│ Cause    prek.toml could not be parsed                                           │
│          Invalid value (at line 12, column 9)                                    │
│ Fix      Fix prek.toml, or regenerate it with `pkgdx init --reset`               │
│ Done     identify project root, identify Git top-level                           │
│ Not run  prek install, prek update --check, detect-secrets scan                  │
╰───────────────────────────────────────── re-run with -d for the full traceback ─╯
step_states: n/a per step. Only one transient line: spinner + '[n/N]' + current label + elapsed (shown after 0.5s). Completed steps don't persist; outcome appears only in the result block.
header: None persistent. The transient status line carries 'pkgdx init [n/N] <step>'.
success_summary: 'pkgdx init: done in <elapsed>' plus one 'changed:' line listing the files created or updated (or 'changed: nothing').
warning_presentation: Collected during the run and printed after the summary line as a compact list: '!' + step label + detail, with a '->' hint on the next line. The heading carries the count ('with 2 warnings'), so it is never colour-only.
failure_presentation: Rich Panel (ROUNDED, red border, title bold) with BLUF title 'error: pkgdx init failed at <step>'. A two-column grid inside gives Cause (detail + message), Fix (hint), Done and Not run. The subtitle points to -d. No traceback for expected errors (a typed StepError / known exception map). Unexpected exceptions print a one-line 'unexpected error' card plus the Rich traceback and an issue-tracker link. Ctrl-C: 'pkgdx init: interrupted during prek update --check, no cleanup performed', exit 130.
state_change_reporting: Only changes are reported: a 'changed:' line aggregates details that are created/updated. Unchanged and reused items stay silent unless -v. This needs a small change-kind field on Result, or classification by keyword.
non_tty_behaviour: No panel, no spinner. GNU-style lines: success 'pkgdx init: done in 2.9s' + 'pkgdx init: changed prek.toml (updated, 2 hooks added)' per change. Warn 'pkgdx init: warning: identify Git top-level: not a Git repository, using project root' + '  hint: Run `git init` ...'. Fail 'pkgdx init: error: configure pre-commit hooks: prek.toml could not be parsed' + '  Invalid value (at line 12, column 9)' + '  hint: Fix prek.toml, or regenerate it with `pkgdx init --reset`' + '  not run: prek install, prek update --check, detect-secrets scan'.
risks: No record of completed steps on success. Users who want to see that the steps ran must use -v (a deliberate trade-off for brevity).
Panel box-drawing characters render in Windows Terminal. Rich falls back to ASCII on legacy_windows, but some fonts misalign wide rows, so narrow terminals wrap the card.

It needs a clear split between expected and unexpected errors (an exception-to-card mapping). If that split is wrong, real bugs get rewritten into friendly cards and their tracebacks are lost without -d.
The error-card helper can be reused by `pkgdx config` and other commands. That only pays off if those commands adopt it; otherwise it is a single-use abstraction (YAGNI).
curation_note: Graft from diagnostic-report (rustc/ruff): inside the error card, use a '= help:' style line for the fix so the card scans like a compiler diagnostic. Warnings on success use the same diagnostic shape, but unboxed.
